intended_object: The canonical homeomorphism X ≃ₜ S(X), x ↦ closure {x}, between a sober space X and its soberification S(X) (the space of irreducible closed subsets, with the topology whose opens are the sets of irreducible closed subsets meeting an open U of X). This shows the unit of the sober reflection is an isomorphism on sober spaces. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: "Sober" is encoded as `[QuasiSober X] [T0Space X]`, which is Mathlib's usual way to say it, so the hypotheses are the right ones. The forward map is `irreducibleSetEquivPoints.symm`, i.e. x ↦ closure {x}, the standard unit map. The inverse sends an irreducible closed set F to its generic point. The topology on `IrreducibleCloseds X` (defined in the same file) is the standard soberification topology: its opens are the sets {F | F ∩ U ≠ ∅} for U open in X. Continuity of the forward map comes from `unit X`. Continuity of the inverse is shown correctly: the generic point of F lies in an open S exactly when F meets S. So the object is the standard canonical homeomorphism, built in its natural generality. Mathlib, at the version this library uses, does not put a topology on `IrreducibleCloseds` and has no such homeomorphism; it only has the order isomorphism `irreducibleSetEquivPoints`.
